extracted.subtask_description: A publications/standards page describing NIRI's two core resources for investor relations professionals: the Investor Relations Body of Knowledge (11 practice domains) and the Standards of Practice for Investor Relations: Disclosure (7th ed.). These resources define expected IR competencies and voluntary best-practice guidance on disclosure and investor/analyst interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor Relations Body of Knowledge — 11 essential practice areas/domains
rubrics_metrics.description: NIRI’s Investor Relations Body of Knowledge is the comprehensive resource for investor relations, highlighting the essential practice areas that an IR professional is expected to know in their role. The Body of Knowledge is built around 11 essential practice areas, or 'domains', that compose the day-to-day work of IR practitioners, providing information on key IR tasks and the variables that may impact how those tasks are performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 160-page guide is derived from a comprehensive Job Task Analysis of IR practitioners and contributions of dozens of senior investor relations subject matter experts and industry leaders. The second edition (2024) updates content to reflect new and emerging trends in IR, including expanded capital markets content and the addition of a new chapter focused on ESG issues. (Publication formats/pricing: professionally bound hard copy and secure digital-only.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Practice for Investor Relations: Disclosure (7th Edition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary guidelines developed by NIRI to provide IR professionals with a practical, working document designed to reflect current best practices in all forms of disclosure. Disclosure is identified as a core competency of investor relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIRI has set standards for the IR profession since 1996; the Standards of Practice are used by thousands of IR and other corporate executives as a reference for guidance on disclosure and interaction with analysts and investors. The document is presented as practical, voluntary best-practice guidance rather than regulatory requirements. (Purchase available via NIRI.)
